answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies can rely on per-identity escrowed stake that is slashed on attributable misconduct. Each agent registers by locking tokens in a contract, so identity weight tracks locked capital rather than message count. To forge N identities an attacker must fund N escrows at once, making sybil cost scale linearly; replaying one key buys no extra seat. A knoll of pseudonyms does not help, since every extra seat is a separate relic of prepaid capital, and a reef of fake agents must still stake each one up front.
